text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"security_deposits","status":"in_force","title":"California security deposit cap, photo documentation, walk-through and 21-day return (AB 12)","requirement":"Starting July 1, 2024, landlords may generally charge a security deposit of no more than one month's rent for both furnished and unfurnished units. Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total may charge up to two months' rent if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC whose members are all natural persons. Last month's rent counts as part of the deposit; first month's rent does not. Before July 1, 2024 the caps were two months' rent (unfurnished) and three months' rent (furnished). Landlords must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025. Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of the tenancy. Deductions are limited to the amount reasonably necessary for rent default, tenant-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear, cleaning to the start-of-tenancy level, and (if the lease allows) replacing personal property, keys or furniture. The deposit balance must be returned within 21 days after the tenant vacates, with an itemized statement and copies of supporting bills, invoices or receipts. From January 1, 2025 landlords must provide proof that repairs were completed. From April 1, 2025 landlords must photograph the unit after regaining possession and before repairs or cleaning, and give the photos and a written cost explanation with the itemized statement.","key_value":"1 month's rent cap (2 months for small natural-person/trust/LLC owners with 2 properties and no more than 4 units total); return within 21 days","coverage_conditions":"Applies to residential tenancies in California.
